newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Central Bank urges Britain to enter EMU.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Central Bank urges Britain to enter EMU.

text.p: Britain should rapidly cast aside its suspicions of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), both for its own benefit and for that of its European partners, the deputy director of the Dutch Central Bank told a conference in London on Tuesday.

"Although the time for a decision... is rapidly approaching, it is still unclear what the United Kingdom will decide. For banks in particular..., early resolution of this issue is essential," Professor Age Bakker said in prepared remarks to the Fifth City of London Banking Conference.

Bakker said the Netherlands and Britain need to adopt a common stance. The two countries are key trading partners and are both advocates of free trade which was best served by stable exchange rates, he said.
The two are also jointly home to a number of multinationals, notably Royal Dutch/Shell and Unilever.
Baker said that common stances should entail membership of EMU, not only for mutual benefit, but for independent gain.

"Rather than dwelling at length on what might go wrong, sceptics would do well to take an objective view of the solutions and safeguards that have been devised to ensure the soundness of the project," Bakker says.
EMU involves joint decision-making rather than the loss of policy-making power, he maintained.

While the British government's indecision has clouded its public and its business and financial sectors with uncertainty, for bankers at least one thing was definite: the increasing importance of the euro and its transformation into a key trading and reserve currency.
"Whether the UK will join or not, we may be sure that here, too - in the very heart of the UK - the euro will claim its share in the exchange markets, once EMU has been established,"
